candidates.title: §7.5 step 5's "archive commit is the run's last one" / "bundle directory... otherwise untouched once archived" invariant is now false and no task updates it
candidates.detail: Step 5 states "commit `takt(<slug>): archive`. That commit is the run's last one" (line 884) and later "there is no write after the archive commit" / "the bundle directory is otherwise untouched once archived" (lines 902-909), describing the only post-archive bundle-write mechanism as a later `next` sweeping dirty files into a *second archive commit*. This diff's `finishOrArchivedOnly` (internal/cli/cmd_verify.go:64) lets `done --step retro` run in `archived`, and `doneRetro`'s own doc comment (internal/cli/cmd_done.go:195-201) plus TestDoneRetroAcceptedInArchivedPhase (internal/cli/finish_test.go, asserting `git log -1` contains "retro done") confirm it lands its own distinct `"retro done"` bundle commit after the archive commit — a mechanism §7.5 step 5 does not describe and one that falsifies both the "last commit" and "untouched once archived" claims for every disposition, not just `keep`. cmd_done.go:200-201's own comment ("design §7.5 step 5 already contemplates post-archive bundle writes") asserts the design doc already covers this, but step 5 only contemplates the second-archive-commit sweep, not an independent `done`-issued commit. No task in this run's plan (docs/takt/lets-work-on-63/plan.md) is scoped to fix step 5's text — task 8 explicitly restricts its edits and verify checks to the `3. **Retro**`–`4. **Disposition**` span of step 3 (plan.md:92-97) — so this contradiction ships undocumented. (Already logged as a follow-up in docs/takt/lets-work-on-63/follow-ups.json at wave 3, but it remains unfixed as of this diff.)

candidates.title: doneRetroChecks' missing/empty-file branch has no test, and its semantics silently changed
candidates.detail: doneRetroChecks (new in this diff) replaced the old fileNonEmpty(retro.md) check with an inline os.ReadFile + strings.TrimSpace(...) == "" check. This is a real behaviour change: fileNonEmpty only checks file size > 0 (facts.go:41-44), so a whitespace-only retro.md previously passed this gate and would have been hashed/recorded; now it is refused as "missing or empty". None of the new tests (TestDoneRetroRefusesUnfilledProseSlot, TestDoneRetroRefusesARecordedRetroInExecute, TestDoneRetroAcceptedInArchivedPhase) or any existing test writes a missing/empty/whitespace-only retro.md while in the finish or archived phase, so this branch and its behaviour change are completely unexercised by the suite.

candidates.title: `got["ignored"] != nil` assertions are tautological on the failure path
candidates.detail: In TestDoneRetroRefusesUnfilledProseSlot (line 306) and TestDoneRetroRefusesARecordedRetroInExecute (line 346), the refusal assertions check `code != 1 || got["ignored"] != nil`. `got` is unmarshalled only from stdout (cmd_init_test.go:17-33), while `fail()` writes exclusively to stderr (cli.go:158-161), so on any refusal (code 1) stdout is empty and `got` is nil — `got["ignored"]` can never be non-nil here. The check adds no real coverage of the 'must not be marked ignored' intent; the actual no-new-receipt guarantee is (correctly) covered separately via countEvents before/after.

verdicts.evidence: Design doc §7.5 step 5 (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-24-takt-design.md:884) says the archive commit 'is the run's last one', and lines 902-909 say 'there is no write after the archive commit' and 'the bundle directory is otherwise untouched once archived', describing only a `takt next`-driven dirty-file sweep into a second `archive` commit. This diff's `finishOrArchivedOnly` (internal/cli/cmd_verify.go:64) lets `done --step retro` run when `st.Phase == bundle.PhaseArchived`, and `doneRetro`/`doneRetroChecks` (internal/cli/cmd_done.go:195-201, 216-219) plus `TestDoneRetroAcceptedInArchivedPhase` (internal/cli/finish_test.go, ending `if s := testutil.Git(t, d.root, "log", "-1", "--format=%s"); !strings.Contains(s, "retro done")`) show `cmdDone`'s own `commitBundle(ctx, tgt.ws, tgt.bdir, tgt.slug, *step+" done")` call (internal/cli/cmd_done.go:81) lands a distinct 'retro done' commit after archive — a mechanism separate from `recommitArchive`'s 'archive'-message sweep (internal/cli/archive.go:97-120). The doc comment at cmd_done.go:200-201 asserts 'design §7.5 step 5 already contemplates post-archive bundle writes,' but step 5's text names only the second-archive-commit sweep. Task 8's scope is confirmed restricted to the step-3 span (docs/takt/lets-work-on-63/plan.md:89-97), and this exact contradiction is already logged, unresolved, in docs/takt/lets-work-on-63/follow-ups.json:142-151 ('Design doc's §7.5 step 5 "archive commit is the run's last one" invariant is now false, and no task in the plan is scoped to fix it').

The claim that 'no ... existing test writes a missing ... retro.md while in the finish or archived phase' is contradicted by the pre-existing, unmodified TestRetroRunInputsAndDone: after driveToFinish (phase stays 'finish') and before retro.md is written, it runs `if code, _, _ := d.cmd("done", "--step", "retro", "--slug", "demo"); code == 0 { t.Fatal("done retro needs retro.md") }` (internal/cli/finish_test.go:510), which exercises exactly the `os.ReadFile` error half of doneRetroChecks' `err != nil || strings.TrimSpace(string(b)) == ""` branch (internal/cli/cmd_done.go:221-224) in the finish phase. The narrower true point — that a whitespace-only (non-zero-length) retro.md's behaviour silently changed from accepted (old `fileNonEmpty`, which only checks `fi.Size() > 0`, facts.go:41-44) to refused, and that no test uses such whitespace-only content — is real, but the candidate's stated claim of total non-coverage of the branch is false.

`fail` (internal/cli/cli.go:158-161) writes its JSON only to `w` (called as `env.Stderr` throughout cmd_done.go), never to stdout. `runIn` (internal/cli/cmd_init_test.go:17-33) only unmarshals `got` from `out.Bytes()` when `out.Len() > 0`; on a refusal nothing is written to stdout, so `got` stays nil, and indexing a nil map (`got["ignored"]`) yields the zero value, so `got["ignored"] != nil` is always false whenever `code == 1`. The two cited assertions — `if code != 1 || got["ignored"] != nil { t.Fatalf(...) }` — appear verbatim in TestDoneRetroRefusesUnfilledProseSlot and TestDoneRetroRefusesARecordedRetroInExecute at internal/cli/finish_test.go:1068 and :1108 (the candidate's cited '306'/'346' are the diff file's own line numbers, not finish_test.go's, but the code and both test names match exactly). Both tests separately assert the real no-new-receipt guarantee via countEvents before/after (finish_test.go:1066/1074 and the analogous lines in the execute-phase test), confirming the `got["ignored"]` half adds nothing.
